recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Future changes to these Permission examples should be made in HL7/data-access-policies; any new Consent work should wait for a final WG decision that accounts for Permission no longer being core.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive with Modification Security WG R6 issue saying Permission and Consent did not address non-patient access-control use cases such as directory access and did not cover resource element-level access control.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-47307. The relevant Permission examples were already present or added through the same example family: R6 ballot Permission had SANER and VhDir examples, commit 9befcacddd1d4d69a926fe60c723c90333e3601a added a directory-admin example, and commit 22d828960244ffa5a3d96df71fe1e3e30e410406 added/listed simple-directory, sensitive-directory, and residual Bundle Permission examples.
additional_context: FHIR-23072 is the tightly related applied patient-agnostic directory/authorization example issue; its comments record Security changed the target from Consent to Permission and its final resolution cites the same SANER, VhDir, simple directory, and sensitive directory examples. FHIR-49908 clarified Permission scope and already has an external-repo audit. Later commit 0e2a8a7f839d5e1a43787523daccf07d958362f3 removed Permission from core and linked Permission to the Data Access Policies IG.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No core source change was made because reintroducing source/permission or adding duplicative Consent prose would be outside current core build scope and contrary to the later Permission move.
